paper_title: Interpretable and Fair Generalized Additive Models
core_problem: Lack of explicit quantitative metrics for evaluating interpretability in NN-based GAMs, and the underexplored simultaneous optimization of interpretability and fairness.
methodology_summary: Proposes a Multi-Objective Neural Basis Model (MONBM) framework based on multi-objective evolutionary learning to simultaneously optimize accuracy, interpretability, and fairness. Introduces explicit quantitative metrics (smoothness and monotonicity) for interpretability.
empirical_results: Reveals complex relationships between accuracy, interpretability, and fairness, demonstrating how multi-objective optimization can be combined with self-interpretable models.
explicit_limitations: Existing research often assumes GAMs inherently provide satisfactory explanations, and traditional regularization techniques influence interpretability implicitly rather than providing explicit quantitative criteria for optimization.
